The emergency PIN is entered instead of the usual one under coercion. It never unlocks NovaGram: it signs out of every account and destroys the local data, after which the application keeps working as an empty client. The Telegram cloud history and the copies held by other people are not removed. It must differ from the usual PIN.

The version number opens the release it was built from, with the list of what changed. Based on Telegram Android %1$s.

Every eight hours NovaGram reads a small file with the latest version from raw.githubusercontent.com. It is the only network request NovaGram makes outside Telegram, and all it reveals is that the client is running: no account and no conversation take part in it. The package is verified against the checksum from the same file, and installing it over the current one keeps all chats and settings. In decoy mode the check does not run at all.

Your own sent messages are removed once the period passes: first the text is replaced with \".\", a minute later the message is deleted for both sides. A message that can no longer be edited is simply deleted, and so is media: replacing a caption would leave the file. Telegram usually allows editing for 48 hours, which is shorter than the period here, so most messages are deleted without the text step.\n\nThe countdown starts when the message is sent. Messages sent before the feature was switched on are not queued; use Erase evidence in the chat menu for those. Chats where you have admin rights are excluded by default, and Saved Messages are never touched.

Only your own traces in this chat are destroyed: outgoing messages through the replace-then-delete steps, together with the files, voice and video messages you sent. The other side\'s messages are left alone.\n\nThe operation cannot be undone.
Reactions are removed from the messages found in this chat. Telegram offers no way to ask the server where this account reacted, so reactions on messages outside the chosen period are not covered.
Destroy your messages and reactions in this chat: %1$s?
Queued for destruction: %1$d. The result follows once the queue is through.

Queued for destruction: %1$d. The chat could not be walked to the end, so older messages in this period were not covered — run it again.

In this dialog NovaGram does not tell the other side that you read their messages: the read marks never appear for them. This is done where a stranger wrote to you and you have not answered yet.

Hiding ends by itself the moment you send anything here, from this device or from another one: answering somebody already tells them you read it. That cannot be undone either.

Side effect: for Telegram the messages stay unread, so the unread counter in this dialog can come back after a restart and on other devices.

Turning it off cannot be undone: once the receipt reaches the server the other side sees the messages as read, and hiding cannot be restored in this dialog. Sending a message here does exactly the same, so there is no need to press this before answering.
The other side cannot see that you read this. Answering here turns it off, as does the chat menu.

When a stranger writes to you and you have not answered yet, NovaGram does not tell them that you read it: the read marks never appear for them. The rule is made when such a message arrives; conversations that were already going before the setting was switched on are left alone. Groups, channels, bots and Saved Messages are never touched.

One thing takes hiding back, and takes it back for good: any message you send into that dialog, from this device or from another one. A draft you did not send and service entries such as a changed photo or a call change nothing.

Side effect: for Telegram the messages stay unread, so the unread counter can come back after a restart and on other devices. Hiding can also be turned off from the menu of a particular dialog, and that cannot be undone.

Between 22:00 and 07:00 in the local time of this device, outgoing messages are sent without a notification sound for the recipient. The message is delivered as usual and is visible in the chat, only the notification becomes silent. A scheduled message is judged by the hour it is due, not by the hour it was written.
Keep notification text off the servers

The text you read in a notification is not written by this device: Telegram composes it on its server, puts it into a push message and hands that to Google for delivery. NovaGram tells the server not to do it. Push then carries the sender's name and nothing else, and the text appears a moment later, taken from the message itself — which this client receives over its own connection anyway. What the notification then shows on this screen is decided by the switch below, not by this one.

What it costs. This is a setting of the account on Telegram's side, not of this device: notification previews go off on your other devices too, and the switch "Show message text" in the official clients will read as off there. The text also arrives a moment after the notification rather than with it, so under battery saving, in Doze or without network it may not arrive at all — and if the switch below is off, that is, the text is normally drawn here, such a notification keeps only the sender's name. The same setting governs the reaction notifications, so a push will not carry the name of whoever reacted either.

What it does not fix. The contents of a push were never readable by Google: they are encrypted with a key that never leaves Telegram and this device. Google still sees that a push was delivered, when, and how large it was. The message itself is stored on Telegram's servers either way. Nor can this client see a per-chat exception set on another device: Telegram does not send that setting down with the chat, so in such a chat the text can still travel inside push.

The text you see in a notification is built here, on this device, out of a message this client already has — there is no network leak on that path, and what the servers put into a push is the switch above. Hiding guards against something else: against whoever can see the screen, and against the system, which keeps a shown notification until it is dismissed.

While this is on, what disappears from a notification is the text of the message: in its place there is a line saying that a message has arrived. The sender, the chat and the notification's avatar stay where they were — they are what tells whether the conversation is worth opening now. Photos, stickers and voice messages are no longer attached to the notification either.

What it costs. Inside the expanded message list the small avatar of the sender goes with the text: Android hangs both on the one flag this is built from, and prising them apart would mean showing an avatar that Telegram's own "message preview" setting hides. The name of the sender is still there.

What it does not fix. It does not hide whom you are talking to: the name and the avatar reach the screen just the same. The in-app popup notification, if you have turned it on, draws the message itself and is not covered by this, and neither are the home screen widgets. Notifications already in the shade are redrawn when this is switched on, but the ones left there by a previous run of the application can no longer be reached.

The PIN will stop being asked for, and the emergency PIN will be removed with it: it can only ever be entered on the PIN screen, and without a PIN there is no such screen. Local data stays where it is. You will be asked for the current PIN.
Enter the current PIN to remove it. The emergency PIN is removed together with it. The entered digits and their count are intentionally hidden.
The application PIN has been turned off.
Every time the app is minimised
Every time the device is locked

The chosen option is the only thing that decides when the PIN is asked for again. What is chosen is what happens: on device lock (the default) the PIN is asked as soon as the phone is locked; on minimising, as soon as you leave the app; after 10 or 60 minutes of inactivity, when the period is up, even if the app stayed open; only at start, once per launch and again after a day, because a process can live for weeks.\n\nInactivity is measured from what the app can see you do — touches, typing, media. The in-app popup, a chat bubble and the share sheet are not counted, so time keeps running there.
